title: Blueberry Crepes with Cream Cheese
excerpt: Delicate homemade crepes filled with a soft cream cheese mixture and topped with a warm sauce of fresh blueberries. A comforting, elegant breakfast.
imageAlt: Golden crepes folded into triangles, filled with cream cheese and topped with a glossy sauce and whole fresh blueberries.

ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons melted butter (plus a little extra for the pan)
1 cup cream cheese at room temperature

steps: In the blender or with a hand whisk, mix the flour, milk, eggs, melted butter and the pinch of salt until you get a thin, smooth, lump-free batter.
Let the batter rest in the fridge for 15 minutes; this rest relaxes the gluten and gives you tender, elastic crepes.
For the filling, beat the cream cheese in a bowl with two tablespoons of honey and the finely grated lemon zest until silky and easy to spread.

In a small skillet over medium-low heat, place a cup and a half of Fresh Pick blueberries together with half a tablespoon of honey and two tablespoons of water. Cook for 4 or 5 minutes, gently pressing some of the fruit so it releases its crimson juice without falling apart completely, taking advantage of the natural juiciness of this fruit grown in the high mountains of Guasca. We use half the usual sweetener because Fresh Pick blueberries have more natural sugar.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and grease it with a thin film of butter. Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter, immediately swirling the pan to cover the entire bottom evenly.
Cook for 1 minute until the edges lift away on their own, flip carefully and brown for 30 more seconds. Repeat with the rest of the batter to make 8 crepes.
Spread two tablespoons of the cheese cream over half of each crepe, then fold into a triangle or roll up like a handkerchief.
Serve right away, two crepes per plate, generously topped with the warm sauce and decorated with the remaining half cup of fresh, natural blueberries.
tips: To keep the bloom (the soft natural whitish coating) of Fresh Pick blueberries intact, keep them refrigerated in their original container and wash them only seconds before adding them to the recipe.
If the crepe batter thickens after resting, add one or two extra tablespoons of milk before pouring it into the pan to make sure the crepes come out thin and flexible.
You can make the crepes the night before, store them stacked with wax paper between each one in an airtight container, and fill them warm the next day.
This recipe uses half the usual sweetener: Fresh Pick blueberries have more natural sugar, so we cut it back. Taste it and, if you prefer it sweeter, add a little more.
